THE_RULE: A saturated GPU proves SOMETHING is computing. Hawking Accelerator evidence requires naming the owning process, its runtime, its representation, and that the plan was SELECTED AND LOWERED by Hawking. Absent that, report UNATTRIBUTED.

FINDING.verdict: THE PREMISE IS NOT SUPPORTED BY PROCESS EVIDENCE. At this measurement no model server on this machine is computing.
FINDING.hawking: ascension_qwen38_resident holds 11.68 GiB of weights at 1.3-1.6% CPU -- LOADED AND IDLE between self-development cycles. Holding weights is not using the GPU.

foreign_servers_that_would_have_to_be_ex.ollama serve: 22 MB resident, 0.0% CPU, /api/ps returns {"models":[]} -- NO model loaded
foreign_servers_that_would_have_to_be_ex.mlx_lm.server: 84 MB resident, 0.0% CPU, no established connections on :9999. 84 MB is far too small to be holding the 4-bit model its argv names, so it is a server shell with nothing resident.

FINDING.why_this_matters_even_though_the_answer_: Had the GPU been saturated, TWO foreign model stacks were running and would have had to be excluded before any of it could be called Hawking. The directive's warning is not hypothetical on this box.
FINDING.what_could_not_be_measured: per-process GPU residency and utilization require sudo powermetrics, which needs a password this must never ask for. Recorded as UNATTRIBUTED rather than estimated. A GPU number with no owner is the same defect class as a receipt whose producer was never checked.

machinery: tools/future/gpu_attribution.py -- reusable, not a one-off measurement. Names every known model server, classifies each as hawking or foreign, samples %CPU over an interval to separate LOADED-AND-IDLE from ACTIVE, and states explicitly what privilege it lacks.
